results.name: descending_vs_ascending_outside_gap
results.description: For sets of >=3 examples shown in strictly monotone order, yes-rate on non-example targets 1-15 outside the span for descending minus ascending presentation; observed differing from null means presentation direction changes outward generalization in a way the model's first-min/last-max edge marking misses (above null: ascending sets restrict more than modelled, or descending less).
results.code:
# name: descending_vs_ascending_outside_gap
# description: For sets of >=3 examples shown in strictly monotone order, yes-rate on non-example targets 1-15 outside the span for descending minus ascending presentation; observed differing from null means presentation direction changes outward generalization in a way the model's first-min/last-max edge marking misses (above null: ascending sets restrict more than modelled, or descending less).
def test_statistic(df):
    X = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.replace(" ", "", regex=False).str.split(",", expand=True)
    X = X.apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").values.astype(float)
    n = (~np.isnan(X)).sum(axis=1)
    mx = np.nanmax(X, axis=1)
    mn = np.nanmin(X, axis=1)
    t = df["target"].astype(int).values
    r = df["rating"].astype(float).values
    is_ex = (X == t[:, None]).any(axis=1)
    dist = np.maximum(mn - t, t - mx)
    d = np.diff(X, axis=1)
    dv = ~np.isnan(d)
    asc = (n >= 3) & ((d > 0) | ~dv).all(axis=1)
    desc = (n >= 3) & ((d < 0) | ~dv).all(axis=1)
    near = (dist >= 1) & (dist <= 15) & ~is_ex
    a = near & desc
    b = near & asc
    if a.sum() == 0 or b.sum() == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(r[a].mean() - r[b].mean())

results.name: singleton_up_down_asym
results.description: For single-example sets with the example in 11-90, yes-rate on targets 1-10 above the example minus targets 1-10 below it; observed above null means people extend a lone example upward more than downward beyond what the model (symmetric ranges) predicts, below null the reverse.
results.code:
# name: singleton_up_down_asym
# description: For single-example sets with the example in 11-90, yes-rate on targets 1-10 above the example minus targets 1-10 below it; observed above null means people extend a lone example upward more than downward beyond what the model (symmetric ranges) predicts, below null the reverse.
def test_statistic(df):
    X = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.replace(" ", "", regex=False).str.split(",", expand=True)
    X = X.apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").values.astype(float)
    n = (~np.isnan(X)).sum(axis=1)
    mx = np.nanmax(X, axis=1)
    mn = np.nanmin(X, axis=1)
    t = df["target"].astype(int).values
    r = df["rating"].astype(float).values
    is_ex = (X == t[:, None]).any(axis=1)
    dist = np.maximum(mn - t, t - mx)
    x = mx
    base = (n == 1) & (x >= 11) & (x <= 90)
    a = base & (t - x >= 1) & (t - x <= 10)
    b = base & (x - t >= 1) & (x - t <= 10)
    if a.sum() == 0 or b.sum() == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(r[a].mean() - r[b].mean())

results.name: wide_vs_narrow_span_outside_gap
results.description: For sets of >=2 examples, yes-rate on non-example targets 1-10 outside the span when the span is >=40 minus when the span is <=15; observed above null means people scale outward generalization with the set's spread more than the model does, below null less.
results.code:
# name: wide_vs_narrow_span_outside_gap
# description: For sets of >=2 examples, yes-rate on non-example targets 1-10 outside the span when the span is >=40 minus when the span is <=15; observed above null means people scale outward generalization with the set's spread more than the model does, below null less.
def test_statistic(df):
    X = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.replace(" ", "", regex=False).str.split(",", expand=True)
    X = X.apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").values.astype(float)
    n = (~np.isnan(X)).sum(axis=1)
    mx = np.nanmax(X, axis=1)
    mn = np.nanmin(X, axis=1)
    t = df["target"].astype(int).values
    r = df["rating"].astype(float).values
    is_ex = (X == t[:, None]).any(axis=1)
    dist = np.maximum(mn - t, t - mx)
    span = mx - mn
    near = (n >= 2) & (dist >= 1) & (dist <= 10) & ~is_ex

    b = near & (span <= 15)
    if a.sum() == 0 or b.sum() == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(r[a].mean() - r[b].mean())

results.name: interior_density_set_size_gap
results.description: For sets with span >=20 whose examples are of mixed parity, yes-rate on interior non-example targets for 3-4 example sets minus 2-example sets; observed above null means sparse (2-example) sets fill their interior less than the model predicts (people need dense examples to generalize across a gap), below null the reverse.
results.code:
# name: interior_density_set_size_gap
# description: For sets with span >=20 whose examples are of mixed parity, yes-rate on interior non-example targets for 3-4 example sets minus 2-example sets; observed above null means sparse (2-example) sets fill their interior less than the model predicts (people need dense examples to generalize across a gap), below null the reverse.
def test_statistic(df):
    X = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.replace(" ", "", regex=False).str.split(",", expand=True)
    X = X.apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").values.astype(float)
    n = (~np.isnan(X)).sum(axis=1)
    mx = np.nanmax(X, axis=1)
    mn = np.nanmin(X, axis=1)
    t = df["target"].astype(int).values
    r = df["rating"].astype(float).values
    is_ex = (X == t[:, None]).any(axis=1)
    dist = np.maximum(mn - t, t - mx)
    Xi = np.nan_to_num(X, nan=-1)
    valid = ~np.isnan(X)
    ev = ((np.mod(Xi, 2) == 0) & valid).any(axis=1)
    od = ((np.mod(Xi, 2) == 1) & valid).any(axis=1)
    inner = (t > mn) & (t < mx) & ~is_ex & ((mx - mn) >= 20) & ev & od
    a = inner & (n >= 3)
    b = inner & (n == 2)
    if a.sum() == 0 or b.sum() == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(r[a].mean() - r[b].mean())

results.name: set_yes_rate_sd
results.description: Standard deviation across sets (with >=20 responses) of each set's overall yes-rate; observed above null means sets differ in how broadly people generalize more than the model predicts (model too uniform in breadth across sets), below null less.

results.name: rule_interior_violator_yes
results.description: Yes-rate on interior (inside min-max span) non-example targets that violate a non-parity arithmetic rule (power series, multiple of 3-12, ends-in-d) shared by all of a >=2-example set's examples; observed above null means people let range-based similarity override such a rule inside the span more than the model, below null that the rule is held more strictly.
results.code:
# name: rule_interior_violator_yes
# description: Yes-rate on interior (inside min-max span) non-example targets that violate a non-parity arithmetic rule (power series, multiple of 3-12, ends-in-d) shared by all of a >=2-example set's examples; observed above null means people let range-based similarity override such a rule inside the span more than the model, below null that the rule is held more strictly.
def test_statistic(df):
    X = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.replace(" ", "", regex=False).str.split(",", expand=True)
    X = X.apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").values.astype(float)
    n = (~np.isnan(X)).sum(axis=1)
    mx = np.nanmax(X, axis=1)
    mn = np.nanmin(X, axis=1)
    t = df["target"].astype(int).values
    r = df["rating"].astype(float).values
    is_ex = (X == t[:, None]).any(axis=1)
    dist = np.maximum(mn - t, t - mx)
    Xi = np.nan_to_num(X, nan=0).astype(int)
    valid = ~np.isnan(X)
    rules = [[2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64], [3, 9, 27, 81], [4, 16, 64], [5, 25], [6, 36], [7, 49], [8, 64], [9, 81], [10, 100]]
    M = np.zeros((len(rules) + 19, 101), dtype=bool)
    for i, rr in enumerate(rules):
        M[i, rr] = True
    k = len(rules)
    nums = np.arange(101)
    for m in range(3, 13):
        M[k] = (nums % m == 0) & (nums > 0); k += 1
    for dd in range(1, 10):
        M[k] = (nums % 10 == dd); k += 1
    memb = M[:, Xi]  # rules x rows x slots
    allm = (memb | ~valid[None, :, :]).all(axis=2)  # rules x rows
    tm = M[:, t]  # rules x rows
    viol = (allm & ~tm).any(axis=0)
    a = (n >= 2) & (t > mn) & (t < mx) & ~is_ex & viol
    if a.sum() == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(r[a].mean())

results.name: outside_same_decade_gap
results.description: For sets of >=2 examples, among non-example targets 1-9 outside the span, yes-rate when the target is in the same decade (1-10, 11-20, ...) as the nearest edge example minus when it crosses into another decade; observed above null means decade boundaries limit generalization more than the model's interval decade bonus captures, below null less.
results.code:
# name: outside_same_decade_gap
# description: For sets of >=2 examples, among non-example targets 1-9 outside the span, yes-rate when the target is in the same decade (1-10, 11-20, ...) as the nearest edge example minus when it crosses into another decade; observed above null means decade boundaries limit generalization more than the model's interval decade bonus captures, below null less.
def test_statistic(df):
    X = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.replace(" ", "", regex=False).str.split(",", expand=True)
    X = X.apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").values.astype(float)
    n = (~np.isnan(X)).sum(axis=1)
    mx = np.nanmax(X, axis=1)
    mn = np.nanmin(X, axis=1)
    t = df["target"].astype(int).values
    r = df["rating"].astype(float).values
    is_ex = (X == t[:, None]).any(axis=1)
    dist = np.maximum(mn - t, t - mx)
    edge = np.where(t < mn, mn, mx)
    same = ((t - 1) // 10) == ((edge.astype(int) - 1) // 10)
    near = (n >= 2) & (dist >= 1) & (dist <= 9) & ~is_ex
    a = near & same
    b = near & ~same
    if a.sum() == 0 or b.sum() == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(r[a].mean() - r[b].mean())
